extracted.intended_audience: public relations, marketing, corporate communications, and corporate governance professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for organizational crisis management and crisis communication — how to prevent, prepare for, respond to, recover from, and learn from public relations failures using case-study lessons and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention (Five-Step Crisis Management Model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct risk assessments to identify potential vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Five-Step model; emphasizes proactive identification of vulnerabilities so crises can be avoided or minimized. The article cites a statistic that 70% of corporate crises could have been avoided with proper planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation (Five-Step Crisis Management Model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop crisis communication plans that include key messaging and spokesperson training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation involves building detailed plans before a crisis hits, training spokespeople, and creating messaging templates so responses are timely and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response (Five-Step Crisis Management Model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Swiftly address the situation, relying on transparency and empathy in communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During response, organizations should acknowledge mistakes quickly, show empathy and accountability, and communicate transparently. Anti-patterns include defensive or minimizing statements (example: United Airlines CEO calling the passenger “disruptive”).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery (Five-Step Crisis Management Model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement strategies to regain public trust and restore reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recovery can include concrete corrective actions and product or policy changes (example: Tylenol recall and tamper-proof packaging) aimed at rebuilding consumer confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning (Five-Step Crisis Management Model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the crisis management process and implement improvements for future readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-crisis review should identify what worked and failed, and translate lessons into updated plans, training, and systems to transform failures into opportunities for growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Identification (Crisis Communication Plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding who needs to hear what and when.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective plans segment stakeholders (customers, employees, investors, regulators, media) and tailor timing and content of messages accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message Development (Crisis Communication Plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crafting key messages to convey compassion and responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key messaging should emphasize empathy, ownership, and next steps. The article highlights messaging that conveys compassion and responsibility as central to successful communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Relations (Crisis Communication Plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing strong connections with media outlets for accurate reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain trusted media relationships to ensure accurate, timely dissemination of official information during a crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Crisis Management Tools and Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage platforms to track and manage communications and responses during crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools like EveryAction and Eventzilla are cited as ways to coordinate responses, track tasks, and manage stakeholder communications in real time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media Monitoring Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor public sentiment and respond to online inquiries in real-time using specialized tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms such as Sprout Social and Brandwatch help detect issues early, prioritize responses, and measure sentiment during and after crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media Responsiveness (Trend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond promptly to social media complaints; prompt responses correlate with faster recovery in public sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites a study that organizations responding promptly to social media complaints experienced a 33% faster recovery in public sentiment. Rapid, appropriate social responses are therefore a key performance metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive vs. Reactive Approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor proactive approaches—training, awareness programs, and drills—over reactive scrambling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive approaches increase readiness and reduce response time; reactive organizations tend to scramble and perform worse. Drills and awareness programs are concrete proactive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empathy and Accountability (Lesson from United Airlines and BP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Swift acknowledgment of mistakes and demonstrable empathy; accept accountability rather than deflect or minimize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show that lack of empathy or defensive comments (e.g., United Airlines' initial statements, BP CEO's tone) worsen public perception. Empathetic, accountable leadership statements are critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and Decisive Action (Lesson from Tylenol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent communication and decisive corrective actions (e.g., recalls, public warnings) restore trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Johnson & Johnson’s fast recall of 31 million bottles, public warnings, and subsequent tamper-proof packaging illustrate how transparent, decisive measures help rebuild reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural Sensitivity and Responsiveness (Recent Case Studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand audience and social context; respond to cultural or inclusion missteps with swift engagement, apology, and dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incidents like Dove’s and H&M’s demonstrate the need for cultural awareness; timely acknowledgment, apology, and open engagement with critics are presented as effective damage-control measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Assessment and Prevention through Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement prevention strategies and proper training to minimize exposure to crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article links prevention and training to crisis avoidance, noting studies that a majority of crises could be avoided with proper planning and prevention strategies.
